eli: hey all, eli here. first week and i'm trying to build the inference runtime from source on a company workstation (Ubuntu 22.04, RTX 6000). followed the quickstart but compile dies during link. any quick tips? :wave:

marco: welcome! paste the top error and output of `which nvcc` + `nvidia-smi`. also are you building in a container or on host?

eli: building on host. `which nvcc` -> /usr/local/cuda-12.2/bin/nvcc, `nvidia-smi` shows Driver 535, CUDA 12.2. top cmake/make error:

```
/usr/local/cuda-12.2/include/nvrtc.h: No such file or directory
CMake Error at third_party/CMakeLists.txt:22 (message):
  NVRTC not found
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
ld: cannot find -lnvrtc
```

ops: nvrtc is part of the toolkit but sometimes packaged separately on enterprise boxes. run `ls -l /usr/local/cuda-12.2/include | grep nvrtc` and `ls -l /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64 | grep nvrtc`. If headers/libs missing, reinstall the CUDA toolkit (not just driver).

eli: ls shows include/nvrtc.h missing, lib64 has libnvrtc.so. but include dir has host_config.h and cuda_runtime_api.h. weird.

marco: weird indeed. could be a partial install or leftover symlink from /opt/cuda. `readlink -f /usr/local/cuda` and `ls -l /opt/cuda` to check. Also check for package-manager installs: `dpkg -l | grep cuda` and `apt list --installed | grep nvidia`.

devex: quick dev tips: 1) prefer the dev-container image when possible (ghcr.io/redwood-inference/dev-container:cuda-12.2), 2) set CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR explicitly when running cmake if multiple installs exist: `cmake .. -DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda-12.2`, 3) ensure /etc/ld.so.conf.d/cuda.conf contains the lib64 path and run `sudo ldconfig` after installing the toolkit. We'll add a small note about incomplete installs to the doc.

eli: `readlink -f /usr/local/cuda` -> /usr/local/cuda-12.2. /opt/cuda exists and is a symlink to an older path that no longer exists. dpkg shows a distro cuda toolkit installed too (nvidia-cuda-toolkit).

marco: distro package (`nvidia-cuda-toolkit`) is known to conflict. remove it: `sudo apt remove --purge nvidia-cuda-toolkit` then reinstall the official toolkit. Also confirm `pkg-config --list-all | grep nvrtc` in case an old pkgconfig points builds to wrong place.

eli: removed the distro package, reinstalled CUDA deb from NVIDIA. now headers present. cmake progresses further but make fails later with `undefined reference to __cudaRegisterFatBinary` during linking.

ops: that symbol is defined in libcudart or libcudart_static. check that /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64/libcudart.so is present. If using static linking, order matters. Try `ldd <failing-binary>` to see missing shared libs. Also ensure you didn't mix static cudnn with dynamic cudart.

eli: libcudart.so is present. ldd shows some unresolved symbols in a third_party lib. build log shows link uses `-L/usr/lib/wsl` path (this machine is bare metal, not WSL) — somehow /usr/lib/wsl got into link flags.

marco: odd. check `echo $LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and any CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE or environment hook. Could be leftover env var from earlier WSL experiments. `env | grep -i wsl` and `grep -R "WSL" ~/.bashrc ~/.profile` to find stray exports.

eli: found an old export in ~/.bashrc adding /usr/lib/wsl to LD_LIBRARY_PATH. removed it, re-sourced, cleaned build and recompiled. build now almost done but failing unit tests due to missing GPU driver kernel module on CI runner (local build passes).

ci-bot: FYI there's currently a flaky CI job (gpu-integration-linux) failing with kernel module load errors on some runners; ticket CI-330 opened.

devex: thanks for the signal, i'll add a CI note to the onboarding doc: "CI runners may not have matching kernel modules; if local build passes but CI fails, open a CI ticket and attach `dmesg` logs`". Also adding checklist to remove stale distro packages before a toolkit install.

ops: if you want, I can allocate a short-lived reproducible VM (containerd + matching kernel) to run the full test matrix. ping here with "ops vm" and i'll create it.

eli: thanks everyone — removing the stale env fixed most issues. i'll open a short PR to add the checklist item about removing distro cuda packages and WSL leftovers. very helpful! :tada:
